items.title: Judge declines to dismiss Suno publicity rights case, as sixteen more musicians join the legal battle
items.excerpt: The judge in the Isbell-led right-of-publicity class action against Suno has denied Suno's motion to dismiss the original lawsuit, days after an amended complaint added 16 plaintiffs.
items.rationale: New court ruling: Suno's motion to dismiss the Isbell publicity-rights suit was denied, so the artist-identity case goes ahead.

items.title: UA Universe: A New Developer Platform and Community for LUNA
items.excerpt: Universal Audio's UA Universe (public beta) lets LUNA users build and share custom workflow add-ons by prompting AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex. Add-on actions are logged in LUNA's undo history, and early tools include swipe-comping and Ableton Live session import.
items.rationale: New platform: a major DAW vendor opens its recording software to add-ons that users vibe-code with AI assistants, with undo-safe actions.

items.title: Cyanite launches its conversational Concierge for music search
items.excerpt: Cyanite, which has used AI to analyse and tag music catalogues for years, launched Cyanite Concierge, a conversational AI search layer for B2B catalogue search (sync, libraries, publishers).
items.rationale: New product: sync teams and libraries can search catalogues by describing what they need in plain language instead of filtering by tags.

items.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users "DJ their art"
items.excerpt: MIT CSAIL's TangiMap uses an AI agent to reprogram mixers and control pads, mapping digital widgets onto physical knobs, buttons and sliders for musical performance and other creative software.
items.rationale: New research system: an agent does the tedious MIDI-controller mapping for performers, turning any mixer or pad into a custom control surface.

items.title: MADlibs: Analyzing the Distribution of Generative Music
items.excerpt: MADlibs measures what text-to-music models will actually produce across the prompt space (their expressive support), using NLP-generated prompts and MIR analysis of the outputs. The stakes are framed for creators and musical culture.
items.rationale: New research method: it maps which styles and musical traits text-to-music generators can and cannot produce, so creators can see the real range of the tools.

dedup.note: RE-PICK: the FL Studio 2026.2 pick (gearnews.com/fl-studio-daw-software) was removed after fact-check found its Gopher AI features came from the July 2026 release (stale) and 2026.2 itself has no substantive AI. Replacement: arXiv MADlibs (2611.31462). It is a distinct paper with no history match; the nearest published item is the 11-19 generative-psychometrics evaluation paper, which takes a different approach (it evaluates the evaluators, while MADlibs maps what models output across the prompt space). Other candidates I considered and rejected: the Australian Joint Select Committee AI report (Music Ally + CMU, one cluster), which ran in books on 11-26; CMU's Tidal analysis, Hypebot's Sonilo opinion piece and the MusicRadar firmware retread, all excluded per the orchestrator; the George Lynch session anecdote, an interview remark with no concrete release from an off-list outlet; arXiv JukeSim (a recommendation-similarity paper, less creator-facing); and the arXiv K-pop singer diarization benchmark (niche, runner-up). Outlets: CMU, Gearnews, Music Ally, MIT News and arXiv, so 5 distinct with 1 each. The accent #2ec5c5 freed by FL Studio goes to the new pick. Orchestrator: grep published_urls.json across all sections for '2611.31462' and 'MADlibs'. I could not read the full file. MADlibs has no og_image, so ax-media needs a figure from the paper.
